cards.text: This psalm doesn't say who wrote it, but it opens with a call: 'Sing to the LORD a new song.' Not the same old tune on repeat, friend. A brand NEW one!

cards.question: The psalm calls for a new song to the LORD. What reason does it give?

cards.text: Those wonders came with a victory. And the psalm is VERY clear about who won it.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says Israel's army gained the LORD the victory.

cards.text: His own right hand and holy arm gained Him the victory. My mustache has packed a LOT of cookie boxes, friend, but it has never won anything bigger than a staring contest with the oven.

cards.question: The LORD doesn't keep His salvation a secret. He has proclaimed it and revealed His righteousness to the ___.

cards.text: Then the psalm looks at Israel. He has remembered His love and faithfulness to the house of Israel, and friend, He remembers a whole lot better than I remember an oven timer.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says only the house of Israel has seen the salvation of our God.

cards.text: Now the psalm turns a corner. It's done telling what the LORD did, and it starts handing out invitations.

cards.question: The psalm calls for a joyful noise to the LORD. Who is it calling to make that noise?
True or false: The psalm wants this praise to the LORD kept soft and quiet.

cards.text: A joyful NOISE, friend, not a perfect one, which is GREAT news for my singing voice. Then the psalm brings in the band, starting with the lyre and the harp.

cards.question: After the lyre and the harp, the psalm turns the volume UP. What joins in next?
Everyone is shouting for joy before the LORD, the King. True or false: The psalm calls on more than people, and invites the sea and all that fills it too.

cards.text: Then the psalm says, 'Let the rivers clap their hands.' Friend, I clap with a MUSTACHE, and even I'm impressed.

cards.question: The rivers aren't the only part of creation joining in. What else does the psalm call to sing together for joy?
The rivers clap and the mountains sing for joy before the LORD. Why? For He comes to ___ the earth.

cards.text: Judgment might sound like the scary part, but here all of creation is singing about it. I think it's because of HOW He judges.

cards.question: How does the psalm say the LORD will judge the world?

cards.text: And the peoples? He judges them with equity. Fair all the way around, friend, and THAT is worth some river applause.

findings.problem: "Those wonders came with a victory" links the wonders and the victory. Psalm 98:1 sets the two clauses side by side but never says how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank quotes the line and blanks its last word ("revealed His righteousness to the ___"). The setup "doesn't keep His salvation a secret" fits nations, priests and elders equally, so the baker is guessing the wording of the line instead of reasoning out its meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 10's question already says the psalm "calls for a joyful noise." That gives away card 11, which asks whether the praise should be kept soft and quiet. Card 11 is a free point and never tests v4's "break forth—let your cry ring out."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Drums and tambourines" includes drums, which do not appear in the BSB. This is a which-thing question, so its wrong answers must be real Bible details.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: "Everyone is shouting for joy before the LORD, the King" turns v6's call ("shout for joy before the LORD, the King") into something already happening. The text gives a call, not a report.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank quotes v9's line and blanks a word ("For He comes to ___ the earth"). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason toward "judge" over "bless" or "water," so it is guessing the wording of the line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: "The rivers clap and the mountains sing for joy before the LORD" turns v8's "Let the rivers clap… let the mountains sing" into something already happening. The text calls on them. It doesn't report them doing it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Here all of creation is singing about it" turns the psalm's calls ("Let the sea resound… let the mountains sing") into an event already happening.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 18 says creation sings because of HOW He judges. That setup rules out the two harsh wrong answers ("With fierce wrath," "With heavy force"). The wrong answers also differ in tone from the right one, so "With righteousness" stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
